drafts.title: $3.64 gas vs my garage fill-up before Thanksgiving

AAA national average regular was $3.6448 on Nov 22. The Thanksgiving Day record is $3.58 (2022). A year ago it was about $3.09.
Xcel Colorado time-of-use (Nov 2026, per GreenCalculus summary of the rate book): 12.72 cents per kWh off-peak vs 31.56 cents on-peak, 5 to 9 p.m. weekdays.
Tesla owner guidance: leaving at 100% is fine if you head out soon after it finishes.

drafts.title: 22 Colorado fast-charger sites funded, not signed
drafts.angle: The money is there, the plugs aren't all there yet. Crowdsource where the Western Slope and I-70 need one.
bullets: CDOT told its Transportation Commission Nov 18: 18 NEVI-funded charging plazas open, 24 in development, 22 awarded but not yet contracted (64 total).
CDOT says Colorado's NEVI money is fully obligated; Round 10 applications due Dec 5, 2026; remaining awards hoped for by mid-2027.
State DCFC Plazas grant this round is about $14 million; ports must deliver at least 150 kW, minimum four per site.
Lyons opened four Level 3 chargers at Sandstone Park Nov 20, battery-backed, run by Jule.
drafts.body: 22. That's how many Colorado fast-charging sites have the money but no signed contract yet. 18 are open. I charge at {my usual I-70 stop} and I'd love one in {town that needs one}. Where on I-70 or the Western Slope do you wish there was a fast charger?
drafts.framework_body:
22.

That's how many Colorado fast-charging sites have been awarded money but still don't have a signed contract, per CDOT this week. 18 are open and 24 more are being built.

Over here on the Western Slope I mostly use {my usual I-70 stop}. A good stop to me is simple: a fast plug, a clean restroom, and somewhere to grab food. Fruita does that right.

Where I'd put the next one: {town that needs one}, because {why}.

Funded isn't the same as plugged in.

Where on I-70 or the Western Slope do you wish there was a fast charger?

drafts.title: 43% would use AI to find the best Black Friday price
drafts.angle: Use AI to check the price, then check the AI. Broad 35-54 and 55+ reach outside the EV niche. Not a scam post (those went live Nov 21).
bullets: YouGov via EMARKETER: 30% of US Black Friday/Cyber Monday shoppers have used AI to help them shop; 27% more would consider it.
43% would use AI to find the best price, 37% to track price changes; only 5% would let it complete a purchase even with approval.
Blue Yonder: 46% of US shoppers have returned something bought after an AI recommendation; 36% because it wasn't as described.
BCG (Nov 4): only 54% trust Black Friday discounts are actually lower than normal.

drafts.title: 4.5 million homes from small reactors with TVA (policy)
drafts.angle: What a small reactor plant is and who it's for, in kitchen-table terms. Honest about what isn't built yet. No politics.
bullets: ENTRA1 (NuScale's commercialization partner) signed Sargent & Lundy Nov 18 to engineer NuScale SMR plants.
Each module is 77 MW; a 12-module plant is 924 MW.
TVA program: up to 6 GW, which the companies say could power about 4.5 million homes or about 60 data centers.
No VOYGR plant has been built yet; cost and build time are still estimates. NuScale cancelled its first Utah project in 2023.
drafts.body: 4.5 million homes. That's what up to 6 GW of small reactors planned with TVA could power, per the companies. None of these plants exist yet and cost is the big question. Would you want a small reactor powering your town?
drafts.framework_body:
4.5 million homes.

That's what up to 6 GW of small nuclear reactors planned with TVA could power, according to the companies. Or about 60 data centers.

Plain version: each module is 77 MW, and a full plant stacks 12 of them for 924 MW.

Here's the catch. None of these plants have been built yet. NuScale's first project in Utah got cancelled in 2023 over cost.

I like the idea of steady power that isn't burning anything. I just want to see what it does to {my monthly electric bill} before I cheer.

Would you want a small reactor powering your town?
drafts.ocr_why: Clear number and a fair take, but no first-hand hook, so it leans on the question.
